# An exact critical residual-row Jensen obstruction on three integer fibers
not OC. It uses n=d=1, a complete integer base, genuinely globally critical
caps, an exact active KKT row, and strictly nonheavy fibers. OC itself is
already covered by the separate d=1 Helly argument.

## 1. The actual source and all-halfspace depth

At bases -1,0,1 take centered intervals

    K_-1=[-1/2,1/2], K_0=[-1,1], K_1=[-5/4,5/4].

Let C be the convex hull of these three embedded intervals. Their actual
sections are exactly these intervals: the piecewise-linear half-width
through1/2,1,5/4 is concave. The complete integer base is {-1,0,1}, and

    V=(1,2,5/2), M=11/2, max V=5/2<11/4=M/2.

At y=(0,0), every containing cap can first be moved to pass through y.
If its continuous normal is nonzero, reflection in x and positive
normalization put it in the form x+a z>=0. Its middle contribution is1.
For the centered interval of radius R write
T_R(t)=min(2R,max(0,R-t)). The endpoint contribution is

    T_(1/2)(a)+T_(5/4)(-a)
      =5/2-[T_(5/4)(a)-T_(1/2)(a)] >=1.

The last difference is the length captured in the set difference of
the two nested intervals, whose total length is3/2. Thus every such
cap has mass at least2. A purely integer closed through-y cap contains
the middle fiber and at least one endpoint, so has mass at least3.
This treats its positive boundary mass explicitly.

For every L>=5/4 the two caps

    H_+(L)={x-Lz>=0}, H_-(L)={-x-Lz>=0}

each have mass2: they capture the entire left fiber, one middle half,
and zero length at the right fiber. They cover every point at base0.
Consequently the maximum raw depth over that fiber is2. At an endpoint
base, a sufficiently large integer tilt isolates any chosen own-fiber
half interval, so its maximum raw mixed depth is its own half-length,
namely1/2 or5/4. Therefore the global maximum is exactly Q=2, attained
at (0,0); its normalized value is4/11, strictly above OC's1/4.

In fact the deepest point is unique. At (0,x) with x!=0, an isolating
cap on its shorter own side has mass1+(1-|x|)=2-|x|<2. Both displayed
caps are therefore genuinely critical at the unique deepest point.

## 2. A complete cap cover and an exact optimal KKT row

Set L=2 in H_+,H_-. Add the two original caps

    G_+={x+4(z-1)>=-1/4},
    G_-={-x+4(z-1)>=-1/4}.

They exclude the entire fibers at -1 and0. On the right fiber their
traces are x>=-1/4 and x<=1/4; each has length3/2 and together they
cover that interval. The H pair covers all fibers at z<=0. Thus these
four actual ambient caps cover S, with budgets2,2,3/2,3/2.

For the one-cap residual program, the obstacle e_z is the minimum of
the residual lengths among these four caps. Directly,

    e=(0,1,1).

The sampled convex-majorant program minimizes h_-1+h_0+h_1 subject to
h>=e and h_-1+h_1>=2h_0. Its minimum is3: every feasible vector has
sum h>=3h_0>=3, and h=(1,1,1) attains it. This optimum need not be
unique; the specified one is enough.

Use the usual finite convex supporting-slope constraints with all slopes
zero at this constant h. All those constraints are tight. With objective
derivatives s_z=1, set the convexity flows

    mu_(0,-1)=mu_(0,1)=1,

all other mu to zero, and obstacle multipliers

    lambda_0=3, lambda_-1=lambda_1=0.

The flow row is barycentric since(-1)+1=0, stationarity is
lambda=s+outflow-inflow, and obstacle complementarity holds at0.
These are therefore exact KKT data for that attained program.
The associated absorbing chain from source0 stops there with probability
1/3 and moves to each endpoint with probability1/3, where it stops.
Its terminal row is exactly uniform on {-1,0,1}.

## 3. Strict failure for the actual globally critical cap

For H_+(2), the residual roots (here roots are lengths because d=1) are

    f_H=(-1:0, 0:1, 1:5/2).

The cap is active at the KKT source0, since f_H(0)=e_0=h_0=1. Nevertheless
its ORIGINAL terminal row gives

    sum_j theta_j f_H(j)=(0+1+5/2)/3=7/6>1=f_H(0).

Thus global criticality, complete integer fibers, nonheavy masses, actual
convex compatibility, and the exact active convex-program KKT conditions
do not restore the unchanged residual-root Jensen inequality through
an empty destination. This is a failure of that row inequality itself,
not merely an unnecessary cost of geometric first-exit reweighting.

There is no repair by choosing another critical cap through this center
while retaining the row. With continuous coefficient normalized to+1,
all such through-center caps have middle mass1, so equality Q=2 requires
T_(5/4)(a)-T_(1/2)(a)=3/2. The longer interval's two outside pieces must
both be captured, forcing a<=-5/4. Reflection gives the same conclusion
for continuous coefficient-1. Pure integer caps are not critical.
Hence every critical cap is one of H_+(L),H_-(L), L>=5/4, and has the
same residual-length array above. Boundary endpoint points have zero
length and do not change any equality.

The numerical gap is exactly1/6. No below-target hypothesis is met.
The next section strengthens the obstruction to every KKT system of
this particular program, not to arbitrary transport constructions.

## 4. Every optimal primal and every KKT choice give the same bad row

At any optimum the objective equals3. Since feasibility gives
h_-+h_+>=2h_0 and h_0>=1, equality forces h_0=1 and h_-+h_+=2.
The endpoint obstacles sum to1<2, so at least one endpoint obstacle
has strict slack and its multiplier lambda is zero.

At an extreme base, a nonnegative convexity-flow row cannot have that
base as its barycenter unless all its outgoing edges vanish. Thus only
base0 has outgoing flow, and its barycenter equation gives
mu_(0,-1)=mu_(0,1)=t. The objective derivatives are identically1,
including at a zero height, so endpoint stationarity gives
lambda_-=lambda_+=1-t. One zero endpoint multiplier therefore forces
t=1, both endpoint multipliers zero, and lambda_0=3. Every optimal
primal/KKT system consequently gives the same uniform canonical row.
Section3 classifies every critical cap, so no joint choice of primal,
KKT multipliers, and critical cap repairs its1/6 residual-root gap.

The assertion also holds for the more natural isolated right midpoint
caps {plus-or-minus x+4(z-1)>=0}. Their budgets are5/4, the obstacles
are e=(0,1,5/4), and h=(3/4,1,5/4) with affine slope1/4 attains3.
The endpoint obstacle sum5/4 is again less than2, so the same argument
applies unchanged. These alternatives concern two specified original
cap covers; no claim is made about every possible cover or objective.
